```sh
kafka token expire
```

Expire a delegation token, immediately by default

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

Without --expiry-time-period-ms, expires the token immediately.

## Before you run

Invalidates token access, immediately by default. Confirm dependent clients have replacement credentials; renewal may not recover an expired token.

## Flags

| Flag                               | Description                                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>`               | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092                |
| `--hmac <string>`                  | the token's hmac, base64 (mutually exclusive with --hmac-stdin) |
| `--hmac-stdin`                     | read the token's hmac (base64) from stdin                       |
| `--expiry-time-period-ms <string>` | ms until expiry (defaults to immediate expiry)                  |
| `--yes`                            | confirm the expiry without an interactive prompt                |

## Examples

```sh
kafka token expire --hmac-stdin --brokers localhost:9092 --yes
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "expiryTimestamp": "1700000000000"
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `5`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
